findings.title: Strict decoding accepts a Score with no bounded rubric
findings.evidence: check_score bounds only legend keys at 112–114. Its upper score bound is conditional on a maximum response level being present (126–136). Empty legend plus omitted probabilities therefore requires only finite score >= 0; it never checks a maximum level or requires a usable rubric.
findings.trigger: Call public SystemOneResponse::decode on {"model":"m","answers":{"q":{"type":"score","score":1e100,"confidence":0.5,"legend":{}}}}. A second example is legend:{} with probabilities:{"99":1.0}, score:99: the level-10 cap applies only to legend keys.
findings.inferred_behavior: Both responses pass the strict per-answer decoder and return typed Score answers outside the documented maximum of ten levels. A matching typed Score request can reject the later numeric bound, but direct decode has no such second pass; extra Score answers accompanying a different valid requested question also receive only this insufficient first pass.
findings.contract: The task requires finite numeric ranges and Score legend bounds before typed decisions return. An omitted probability distribution is a supported legacy shape, but that does not justify an unbounded score when the response supplies no usable rubric.
findings.execution: Static source inference only; no decoder, candidate, or checker execution.

findings.title: Request-aware validation uses the pre-override question set
findings.evidence: SystemOneRequest documents that extra_body replaces SDK-written fields (56–58). body() serializes self.questions (135–138), then merges extra_body last (140–142). The existing system_one entrypoint sends that prepared body but validates the response against request.questions, which can differ from the wire questions.
findings.trigger: Construct a valid request with question q of type Noul, then supply extra_body.questions.q as a valid Choice over a and b. Return a valid Choice answer for q.
findings.inferred_behavior: The checked API rejects the valid Choice reply because the original field still says Noul. Conversely, a valid Noul response is accepted although the actual sent question was Choice. The blocking wrapper shares the same path.
findings.contract: The task requires request-aware answer type, coverage, and identity checks. The supported last-write body override must either be accounted for by validation or explicitly rejected before sending at this strict boundary.
findings.execution: Static source inference only; no HTTP or candidate execution.

tests: No material assertion removal or relaxation found. Existing fixture question IDs, Choice names, and level counts now match the served response. Existing assertions continue checking those values. Two array/null-state transport cases switch to system_one_unchecked (tests/client.rs:1513 and 1516), preserving request-body assertions but removing direct checked-path coverage for those cases. Six new integration tests cover malformed values, compatible selected-answer cases, request-aware validation, and async/blocking boundaries. The two counterexamples above are absent from those new cases.
scope: Seven changed/added files stay under crates/jev. No checker files, unrelated packages, dependencies, deletions, or existing-file modes changed. New validator and integration test files use mode 0600.
limits: Unlike the other two SDK packets in this batch, this candidate wires request-aware validation into existing system_one, with explicit unchecked and raw compatibility paths. Non-argmax selected answers, fractional scores, and legacy Score without probabilities are preserved; no requirement that confidence equal the selected probability was imposed in this review. Its probability tolerance grows with the number of rounded entries; that documented policy was not labeled a defect solely because it is permissive. These static findings do not change frozen primary acceptance scores.
